answer: One effective defence is a stake-weighted reputation atlas: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and its history is recorded in that atlas. Creating many fake identities then costs real capital each, while honest agents build reputation that lowers their fees over time. New accounts start with a whisper of trust - a tiny transaction limit - and only earn larger limits after verified work. Like shale layers that form only under long pressure, trust accrues slowly, so an attacker splitting stake across thousands of Sybils gains nothing over one well-behaved identity.
